Now I have comprehensive information. Let me write a complete answer based on my research.

## Understanding HTML's `async` and `defer` Script Attributes

The `async` and `defer` attributes on HTML `<script>` elements fundamentally change when and how scripts are fetched and executed, offering crucial control over page loading performance.

### How `async` Works

For external classic scripts (those with a `src` attribute), the `async` attribute tells the browser to fetch the script in parallel with HTML parsing. According to the WHATWG specification, "if the async attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes)." This means the script may finish downloading while the HTML parser is still working, and execution happens immediately upon completion, potentially interrupting DOM construction. As web.dev notes, "Scripts with async can still block HTML parsing."

A critical characteristic of async scripts is that they do not maintain execution order. When multiple async scripts are present, "It is possible (and likely) that async scripts won't run in the order in which they appear in the HTML."

Regarding the DOMContentLoaded event, async scripts execute before it fires, but the event does not wait for them. According to MDN, "DOMContentLoaded is fired after the execution of these scripts, but before the execution of scripts with async," meaning DOMContentLoaded fires once parsing completes and deferred/module scripts finish, regardless of async script status.

### How `defer` Works

The `defer` attribute specifies that a script should execute after the document is fully parsed. The WHATWG specification states: "If the async attribute is not present but the defer attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched in parallel and evaluated when the page has finished parsing."

Unlike async, deferred scripts maintain execution order. MDN confirms: "Scripts with the defer attribute will execute in the order in which they appear in the document." This is essential when scripts depend on each other or on the DOM being complete.

Importantly, deferred scripts block the DOMContentLoaded event. MDN states that "Scripts with the defer attribute will prevent the DOMContentLoaded event from firing until the script has loaded and finished evaluating." The DOMContentLoaded event fires after all deferred scripts complete execution.

### Inline Scripts vs. External Scripts

The `async` and `defer` attributes have **no effect** on inline scripts (scripts without a `src` attribute). MDN explicitly warns: "This attribute must not be used if the src attribute is absent (i.e., for inline scripts) for classic scripts, in this case it would have no effect." The same restriction applies to `defer`. Inline scripts execute immediately and block HTML parsing.

### Module Scripts

Module scripts (using `type="module"`) behave differently. They defer by default, meaning they wait for parsing to complete before executing. The WHATWG specification explains: "For module scripts, if the async attribute is present, then the module script and all its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing, and the module script will be evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes). Otherwise, the module script and its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated when the page has finished parsing. (The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts.)"

This means:
- Without `async`, module scripts automatically defer (no need to specify `defer`)
- With `async`, module scripts execute as soon as available, like classic async scripts
- The `defer` attribute is ignored on module scripts

MDN confirms: "The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts — they defer by default." Inline module scripts also defer automatically.

Module scripts participate in DOMContentLoaded: "The DOMContentLoaded event fires when the HTML document has been completely parsed, and all deferred scripts (<script defer src=\"…\"> and <script type=\"module\">) have downloaded and executed."

### Summary Table

| Script Type | Parsing | Execution Timing | Execution Order | DOMContentLoaded |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic (no attributes) | Blocks | Immediate | N/A | Waits for completion |
| Classic async | Parallel | ASAP after download | Not guaranteed | Fires before async completes |
| Classic defer | Parallel | After parsing | Guaranteed (document order) | Waits for completion |
| Inline (any type) | Blocks | Immediate | N/A | Waits for completion |
| Module (no async) | Parallel | After parsing (deferred by default) | Guaranteed | Waits for completion |
| Module async | Parallel | ASAP after download | Not guaranteed | Fires before async completes |
